arxiv-2012-08846.title: CP violation from charged Higgs bosons in the three Higgs doublet model
arxiv-2012-08846.creator: Heather E. Logan, Stefano Moretti, Diana Rojas-Ciofalo, and Muyuan Song
arxiv-2012-08846.description: Abstract We demonstrate a new type of cancellation of contributions to the electron and neutron electric dipole moments (EDMs) that occurs in three Higgs doublet models (3HDMs) when CP violation appears in the charged Higgs sector. The cancellation becomes exact when the two physical charged Higgs bosons in the model are degenerate in mass.

arxiv-2102-02873.title: Optimal Construction of Hierarchical Overlap Graphs
arxiv-2102-02873.creator: Shahbaz Khan
arxiv-2102-02873.description: Abstract Genome assembly is a fundamental problem in Bioinformatics, where for a given set of overlapping substrings of a genome, the aim is to reconstruct the source genome. The classical approaches to solving this problem use assembly graphs, such as de Bruijn graphs or overlap graphs , which maintain partial information about such overlaps.

arxiv-2104-11884.title: Social Distancing via Social Scheduling
arxiv-2104-11884.creator: Deepesh Kumar Lall, Garima Shakya, Swaprava Nath
arxiv-2104-11884.description: Abstract Motivated by the need of social distancing during a pandemic, we consider an approach to schedule the visitors of a facility (e.g., a general store). Our algorithms take input from the citizens and schedule the store’s discrete time-slots based on their importance to visit the facility. Naturally, the formulation applies to several similar problems.

arxiv-2310-13421.title: Tensorized Pauli decomposition algorithm
arxiv-2310-13421.creator: Lukas Hantzko, Lennart Binkowski, Sabhyata Gupta
arxiv-2310-13421.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel general-purpose algorithm for Pauli decomposition that employs matrix slicing and addition rather than expensive matrix multiplication, significantly accelerating the decomposition of multi-qubit matrices. In a detailed complexity analysis, we show that the algorithm admits the best known worst-case scaling and more favorable runtimes for many practical examples.

arxiv-2311-16544.title: Multi-Irreducible Spectral Synchronization for Robust Rotation Averaging
arxiv-2311-16544.creator: Owen Howell 1 3 , Haoen Huang 2 , and David Rosen 1 2
arxiv-2311-16544.description: Abstract Rotation averaging (RA) is a fundamental problem in robotics and computer vision. In RA, the goal is to estimate a set of N N unknown orientations R 1 , … , R N ∈ S ​ O ​ ( 3 ) R_{1},...

arxiv-2403-19820.title: Evaluating Explanatory Capabilities of Machine Learning Models in Medical Diagnostics: A Human-in-the-Loop Approach
arxiv-2403-19820.creator: José Bobes-Bascarán, Eduardo Mosqueira-Rey, Ángel Fernández-Leal, Elena Hernández-Pereira, David Alonso-Ríos, Vicente Moret-Bonillo, Israel Figueirido-Arnoso, Yolanda Vidal-Ínsua
arxiv-2403-19820.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by José Bobes-Bascarán, Eduardo Mosqueira-Rey, Ángel Fernández-Leal, Elena Hernández-Pereira, David Alonso-Ríos, Vicente Moret-Bonillo, Israel Figueirido-Arnoso, Yolanda Vidal-Ínsua. This paper presents a comprehensive study on the evaluation of explanatory capabilities of machine learning models, with a focus on Decision Trees, Random Forest and XGBoost models using a pancreatic cancer dataset. We use Human-in-the-Loop related techniques and medical guidelines as a source of domain knowledge to establish the importance of the different features that are relevant to establish a pancreatic cancer treatment.

arxiv-2404-02834.title: Hodge numbers of hypergeometric data
arxiv-2404-02834.creator: Ling Long, Yifan Yang
arxiv-2404-02834.description: Abstract . In this paper, based on the toric hypergeometric model given in a paper by Beukers–Cohen–Mellit, we provide two other ways to explain why the zig-zag diagram method can be used to compute Hodge numbers for hypergeometric data defined over ℚ \mathbb{Q} . 1.

arxiv-2404-14213.title: An Exposure Model Framework for Signal Detection based on Electronic Healthcare Data
arxiv-2404-14213.creator: Louis Dijkstra, Tania Schink, Ronja Foraita
arxiv-2404-14213.description: Abstract Despite extensive safety assessments of drugs prior to their introduction to the market, certain adverse drug reactions (ADRs) remain undetected. The primary objective of pharmacovigilance is to identify these ADRs (i.e., signals). In addition to traditional spontaneous reporting systems (SRSs), electronic health (EHC) data is being used for signal detection as well.

arxiv-2404-19575.title: On the non-existence of oscillation numbers in Sturm-Liouville theory
arxiv-2404-19575.creator: Angelo B. Mingarelli
arxiv-2404-19575.description: Abstract Abstract. We prove an old conjecture that relates the existence of non-real eigenvalues of Sturm-Liouville Dirichlet problems on a finite interval to the non-existence of oscillation numbers of its real eigenfunctions, [ [ 6 ] , p.104, Problems 3 and 5].

arxiv-2502-12906.title: High dimensional hyperbolic Coxeter groups that virtually fiber
arxiv-2502-12906.creator: Jean-François Lafont, Barry Minemyer, Gangotryi Sorcar, Matthew Stover, Joseph Wells
arxiv-2502-12906.description: Abstract This paper provides an iterative procedure for constructing hyperbolic Coxeter groups that virtually fiber over ℤ \mathbb{Z} that is flexible enough to yield infinitely many isomorphism classes in each virtual cohomological dimension (vcd) n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 .

arxiv-2510-19681.title: On a refinement of the Ahlswede–Katona Theorem
arxiv-2510-19681.creator: Jianfeng Hou, Xizhi Liu, Yixiao Zhang
arxiv-2510-19681.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jianfeng Hou, Xizhi Liu, Yixiao Zhang. A classical theorem of Ahlswede and Katona [ AK78 ] determines the maximum density of the 2 2 -edge star in a graph with a given edge density. Motivated by its application in hypergraph Turán problems, we establish a refinement of their result under the additional assumption that the graph contains a large independent set in which every vertex has high degree.

arxiv-2511-01506.title: Derivative-Aligned Anticipation of Forbush Decreases from Entropy and Fractal Markers
arxiv-2511-01506.creator: Juan D. Perez-Navarro a,1 and D. Sierra-Porta a,∗
arxiv-2511-01506.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Juan D. Perez-Navarro a,1 and D. Sierra-Porta a,∗. We present a feature–based framework to anticipate Forbush decreases (FDs) from one–minute neutron–monitor data by tracking sliding–window invariants grounded in information theory, scaling, and geometry. For each station and event, we compute marker time series (Shannon, spectral, permutation, sample and approximate entropy; Lempel–Ziv complexity; Hurst via detrended fluctuation analysis; correlation dimension; Higuchi, Katz, and Petrosian fractal dimensions), smooth them with an exponentially weighted moving average, and analyze their within–station standardized derivatives relative to the time of

arxiv-2601-06873.title: Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search
arxiv-2601-06873.creator: Mustafa Abdool, Soumyadip Banerjee, Moutupsi Paul, Do-kyum Kim, Xiaowei Liu, Bin Xu, Tracy Yu, Hui Gao, Karen Ouyang, Huiji Gao, Liwei He, Stephanie Moyerman, Sanjeev Katariya, [1ex] Airbnb, Inc, USA
arxiv-2601-06873.description: Abstract The goal of Airbnb search is to match guests with the ideal accommodation that fits their travel needs. This is a challenging problem, as popular search locations can have around a hundred thousand available homes, and guests themselves have a wide variety of preferences.

arxiv-2601-14214.title: The PAIRS project: a global formation model for planets in binaries Preprint: J. Venturini
arxiv-2601-14214.creator: Julia Venturini, Arianna Nigioni, Maria Paula Ronco, Natacha Jungo, Alexandre Emsenhuber
arxiv-2601-14214.description: Abstract Binary stars are as common as single stars. The number of detected planets orbiting binaries is rapidly increasing thanks to the synergy between transit surveys, Gaia and high-resolution direct imaging campaigns. However, global planet formation models around binary stars are still underdeveloped, which limits the theoretical understanding of planets orbiting binary star systems.

arxiv-2602-11931.title: AdaptEvolve: Improving Efficiency of Evolutionary AI Agents through Adaptive Model Selection
arxiv-2602-11931.creator: Pretam Ray, Pratik Prabhanjan Brahma, Zicheng Liu and Emad Barsoum
arxiv-2602-11931.description: Abstract Evolutionary agentic systems intensify the trade-off between computational efficiency and reasoning capability by repeatedly invoking large language models (LLMs) during inference.This setting raises a central question: how can an agent dynamically select an LLM that is sufficiently capable for the current generation step while remaining computationally efficient?

arxiv-2605-27890.title: Mid-Infrared Single-Photon Compressive Spectroscopy
arxiv-2605-27890.creator: Ben Sun, Kun Huang, Huijie Ma, Jianan Fang, Tingting Zheng, Ruiyang Qin, Yongyuan Chu, Hairun Guo, Yan Liang, Heping Zeng

pmc-10537693.title: Colorimetric RT-LAMP Detection of Multiple SARS-CoV-2 Variants and Lineages of Concern Direct from Nasopharyngeal Swab Samples without RNA Isolation
pmc-10537693.creator: Santiago Werbajh, Luciana Larocca, Carolina Carrillo, Fabiana Stolowicz, Lorena Ogas, Sergio Pallotto, Solange Cassará, Liliana Mammana, Inés Zapiola, María Belén Bouzas, Adrian A Vojnov
pmc-10537693.description: Since, during the Coronavirus disease 19 (COVID-19) pandemic, a large part of the human population has become infected, a rapid and simple diagnostic method has been necessary to detect its causative agent, the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome-related Coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2), and control its spread.

pmc-10571840.title: Review of Outcomes after Salvage Surgery for Recurrent Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck
pmc-10571840.creator: Dana M Hartl, Joanne Guerlain, Philippe Gorphe, Madan Kapre, Neeti Kapre Gupta, Nabil F Saba, K Thomas Robbins, Ohad Ronen, Juan P Rodrigo, Primož Strojan, Antti A Mäkitie, Luiz P Kowalski, Jatin P Shah, Alfio Ferlito, Gino Marioni
pmc-10571840.description: Simple SummaryLocal recurrences, isolated regional recurrences, and loco-regional recurrences are frequent after treatment for advanced stage head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Salvage surgery may be possible in selected patients, taking into account the location and stage of the recurrent disease, patient age and comorbidities, tumor HPV status, and functional sequelae in relation to initial therapy.

pmc-10615528.title: Delayed discharge from post-anesthesia care unit: A 20-case retrospective series
pmc-10615528.creator: Xiaohui Liu, Yimin Zhang, Xingzhi Cai, Huili Kan, Ailan Yu
pmc-10615528.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Objective:To summarize the characteristics of patients with delayed discharge from the post-anesthesia care unit and to analyze the factors and outcomes of delayed discharge.Methods:Twenty cases of delayed discharge from the PACU (PACU stay >2 hours after surgery) of the main operating room in Liaocheng People’s Hospital, a class A tertiary comprehensive hospital, between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2022, among 28,084 patients who were transferred to the PACU from the operating rooms after surgery, were retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-11360531.title: Fabrication of a Microfluidic-Based Device Coated with Polyelectrolyte-Capped Titanium Dioxide to Couple High-Performance Liquid Chromatography with Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry for Mercury Speciation
pmc-11360531.creator: Ji-Hao Chen, Yu-Ting Luo, Yi-An Su, Yan-Ren Ke, Ming-Jay Deng, Wei-Yu Chen, Cheng-Yu Wang, Jia-Lin Tsai, Cheng-Hsing Lin, Tsung-Ting Shih, Fang-Chi Hsu, Shu-Ling Huang, Chi-Ping Li
pmc-11360531.description: Mercury (Hg) is a toxic element which impacts on biological systems and ecosystems. Because the toxicity of Hg species is highly dependent on their concentration levels and chemical forms, the sensitive identification of the chemical forms of Hg—i.e., Hg speciation—is of major significance in providing meaningful information about the sources of Hg exposure.

pmc-11505653.title: Fusing Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Anti-Cancer Drug Discovery
pmc-11505653.creator: Christos Adamopoulos, Kostas A Papavassiliou, Athanasios G Papavassiliou
pmc-11505653.description: ancer therapies. AI’s ability to simulate human cognitive processes, in combination with ML, offers new opportunities for identifying novel drug targets, predicting patient responses, and conquering cancer drug resistance [1,2,3,4]. AI models using deep learning have already shown success in accurately predicting drug sensitivity and resistance across various cancer types, enabling more personalized treatment approaches [1].

pmc-11508135.title: Formation and Applications of Typical Basic Protein-Based Heteroprotein Complex Coacervations
pmc-11508135.creator: Yufeng Xie, Qingchen Liu, Yubo Ge, Yongqi Liu, Rui Yang, Youling Xiong
pmc-11508135.description: Lactoferrin, lysozyme, and gelatin are three common basic proteins known for their ability to interact with acidic proteins (lactoglobulin, ovalbumin, casein, etc.) and form various supramolecular structures. Their basic nature makes them highly promising for interaction with other acidic proteins to form heteroprotein complex coacervation (HPCC) with a wide range of applications.

pmc-12549791.title: Mortality among law enforcement officers in the United States: a population-wide analysis of the National Occupational Mortality Surveillance data, 2020–2023
pmc-12549791.creator: Peter T Tanksley, JC Barnes, J Pete Blair, M Hunter Martaindale
pmc-12549791.description: SummaryBackgroundLaw enforcement officers (LEOs) face unique occupational hazards that can influence both timing and causes of death. Our objective was to deliver the most comprehensive, population-based portrait of mortality among LEOS in the U.S.—capturing when, why, and among whom deaths occur.

pmc-13312482.title: Patient-derived tumor organoids for personalized cancer immunotherapy: An immunopeptidome-to-validation approach in RCC and BC
pmc-13312482.creator: Gabriella Antignani, Michaela Feodoroff, Jacopo Chiaro, Sara Feola, Salvatore Russo, Firas Hamdan Hissaoui, Manlio Fusciello, Federica D’Alessio, Paolo Bottega, Yvonne Giannoula, Milda Sakalauskaite, Janita Sandberg, Miska Kosonen, Virpi Stigzelius, Tamara J. Luck, Valentina Ferrari, Daniele Ciampi,
pmc-13312482.description: Immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, yet clinical success remains limited, with only a fraction of patients responding. Tumor heterogeneity and patient-specificity hinder response prediction, emphasizing the need for human-based models that accurately reproduce tumor-immune interactions. Conventional preclinical platforms, such as murine models, lack the human-specific HLA-TCR complexity, limiting their ability to accurately evaluate immunotherapy responses.
